newsitem.title: USA: Vermont town rejects school budget.
newsitem.headline: Vermont town rejects school budget.

text.p: Chittenden voters rejected their town's school budget for the third-time this year.
In voting Tuesday, a $1.8 million spending plan failed by a two-to-one margin, 265-to-119.
David Smith, one of three members on the Chittenden school board, said voters rejected the budget because it was just too expensive.
"I think they just rejected the total amount because it was too many dollars," Smith said. " But we're going to have to regroup."
With no high school of its own, Chittenden sends its students to other schools in surrounding Rutland County, with a majority choosing public schools, including Rutland High School.
The town allows the students to chose their schools and 15 have chosen a Catholic high school, Mount Saint Joseph Academy in Rutland.

Vermont state officials, citing separation of Church and state grounds, have threatened to withhold more than $100,000 in edcuation aid for Chittenden if it continues to allow the students to go to Mount Saint Joseph.
A court hearing on the issue has been scheduled for October. --Boston bureau, 617-367-4106
